Method of Attack: Uses malicious Word document templates that trick recipients into enabling macros
Macros launch PowerShell commands to download and install the Emotet Trojan and possibly other malware
Spam emails use reply-chain and direct emails pretending to be fake invoices, order confirmations, payment confirmations, and shipping issues
New document template pretends to be Microsoft Office Activation Wizard to prompt enabling macros
Once infected, sends further spam emails to victim's contacts and downloads other malware
Attack Vector: Malicious email attachments with Word document templates containing macros
Indicators of Compromise: Emails prompting to click Enable Editing and Enable Content buttons
PowerShell command connecting to remote site to download Emotet Trojan to victim's %UserProfile%
Spam emails appearing from known senders or as replies to existing emails
